x-body: Every single-DTO POST wraps its payload as {"request": {...}}; see MutationRequestInterface.

post.description: A confirmation token is spent when the publish is accepted, also when the plan needed none; a publish refused before that leaves it usable. 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED when the plan needs a token and none was sent; 409 CONFIRMATION_INVALID when the token sent is unknown, malformed, spent, of another draft, or no longer matches the plan: prepare again and ask again. Publishing needs Edit Form Scripts (MageMe_WebForms::api_v1_forms_scripts) when the draft brings in markup that runs code on the storefront, or changes markup that already runs, in a text of the form or an HTML field printed as it is, by the rules of the draft commands: without it the answer is 403 ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED with details {key, store_id, parts} and nothing is published. Markup the draft leaves as it was does not stop it; switching on a field or section that holds such markup brings it in.

remove-field takes the confirmation token of the plan like publish does: 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED without one when it is needed, 409 CONFIRMATION_INVALID for an unknown, malformed or spent one. update-form takes the token of prepare-update-form the same way when it writes a live setting whose schema `write` is "confirm" or "script" (a "script" setting also needs MageMe_WebForms::api_v1_forms_scripts; a "none" setting is refused with 400). It also takes one when submitter_email_field_id changes whom a switched-on notification with a submitter source sends to: changes then holds {key: "submitter_email_field_id", kind: "recipients_change", subject {entity, id, name}, detail {recipients [{store_id, source, field_code, role, before, after}]}}, as recipients_change in the publish plan. The answer or refusal of prepare-update-form and prepare-remove-field is not kept, since the answer carries a token: a retry under the same request_id answers 409 REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE, so each prepare goes out under a new request_id.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Submissions per page; a larger value is cut to 100.

422.description: Conflicting id and code, an ambiguous code, or an update naming no field of the form

post.summary: Submit the form, or update one of its submissions (3.x route)
post.description: Each key of `field` (and of `field_other`, the text typed for an Other option) is a field id or a field code. An integer key is an id and is passed on as it is. Any other key is the code of an active field of this form, matched exactly (case-sensitive) after trimming; a code that names no such field is ignored, as an unknown id is. The same field sent by id and by code must carry the same value (numbers and booleans compared as strings, strings trimmed, null equal to "", list order ignored); the first of them is submitted. With `result_id` the submission is updated; only the fields sent are changed, the others keep their values. Answers that fail validation come back as 200 with `success: false` and `errors`. 422 answers, given only to a caller the form is open to: VALIDATION_FAILED with details {field_id, code} when an id and a code of one field carry different values; AMBIGUOUS_REF with details {entity, ref, candidate_ids} when a code belongs to several active fields of the form (send that value by id); VALIDATION_FAILED with empty details when an update (`result_id`) names no field of the form by code and nothing else.

field.description: Answers keyed by field id or field code

field_other.description: Other-option text keyed by field id or field code

result_id.description: The submission to update; omit to create one

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous read, passed back unchanged. Omit to start from the beginning.

get.summary: Submissions of this form that changed, oldest first, resumable through next_cursor

post.description: Switching a form on needs Edit Form Scripts (MageMe_WebForms::api_v1_forms_scripts) when a text of the form runs code on the storefront: a switched-on HTML field in a switched-on section (or in none) printed as it is, or the description, success message or text under the form (a script, an event handler, a javascript: address, a directive other than var, if, depend and trans in the form texts, and other than store url, store direct_url, view url and media url with no other parameter; in an HTML field any directive but store url, store direct_url and media url with no other parameter inside a quoted attribute value): without it the answer is 403 ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED with details {key, store_id, parts} and the form stays off; grant the permission or switch the form on in the admin. Switching a form off never needs it, so an integration without the permission can switch such a form off but not back on. A field or section that is off runs nothing until it is switched on, and switching it on in a draft, through restore-version or by publishing takes the permission.

Copying a form needs Edit Form Scripts (MageMe_WebForms::api_v1_forms_scripts) when a text of the form runs code on the storefront, as for activate: without it the answer is 403 ACTOR_NOT_ALLOWED with details {key, store_id, parts} and no copy is made; grant the permission or copy the form in the admin.

set-content changes the message a store view shows at once only when it does not change; a change answers 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with {changes: {changed, length {before, after}, links {added, removed}}} unless it carries the confirmation_token of prepare-set-content, which takes the same body, writes nothing and answers {confirmation_ref, store_code, requires_confirmation, confirmation_token, expires_at, changes}.
Opens the form's draft, or returns the one already open. 409 CONFLICT when another change to this form holds it: retry shortly, with the same request_id.

update, set-content, set-store-settings and set-conditions on a switched-on notification that change what it sends or to whom answer 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with {notification_id, changes} unless they carry the confirmation_token of the matching prepare-<command>; prepare-<command> takes the same body, writes nothing and answers {notification_id, command, requires_confirmation, confirmation_token, expires_at, changes}. 409 CONFIRMATION_INVALID for an unknown, malformed, spent or mismatched token.
install-preset with an unknown `code` answers 404 NOT_FOUND, as does any command on a form that does not exist.

Body as for mass-status (items_json, status_code). impact_json: {notifies_customer, status {code, label}, email_template, notifications [{id, name}], count (submissions), recipients (the first 10 masked addresses that get a notification)}. When the status emails the customers, mass-status answers 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED unless it carries this confirmation_token; the token is bound to the status code, the listed submissions and the mail: if the status starts or stops emailing the customers, its template, its notifications or the recipients change before the command, mass-status answers 409 CONFIRMATION_INVALID and a new prepare is needed. A status that a form of the listed submissions does not take is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, as mass-status refuses it, and no token is issued.

parameters.name: grantId
parameters.description: A grant carrying the sys:filenames scope. Not needed by a caller holding Disclose Personal Data.

post.description: Body {approval}: not_approved, pending or approved; takes Approve Results on top of Edit Submissions. impact_json: {notifies_customer, approval {from, to}, notifications [{id, name}] (the switched-on notifications that go to the submitter, or to an address the visitor typed into a field, on this change), registers_customer, count, recipient (masked), result_revision}; {notifies_customer: false, result_revision} when the customer gets nothing. When the approval emails the customer or registers a customer account, set-approval answers 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with the same details unless it carries this confirmation_token; the token is bound to the approval, the submission revision and the mails it confirms: a notification switched on or off since the prepare makes it CONFIRMATION_INVALID.

impact_json: {notifies_customer, status {code, label}, email_template, notifications [{id, name}] (the switched-on status-changed notifications that answer this status and go to the submitter or to an address the visitor typed), count, recipient (masked), result_revision}. When the status emails the customer, set-status answers 409 CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED with the same details unless it carries this confirmation_token; the token is bound to the status code, the submission revision and the mail: if the status starts or stops emailing the customer, its template, its notifications or the recipient change before the command, set-status answers 409 CONFIRMATION_INVALID and a new prepare is needed. A status the form does not take (custom statuses switched off on the form, a status being removed, one outside the form's set) is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED, as set-status refuses it, and no token is issued.

values_json.description: The submission's answers: {"fields":[{"field_id":12,"code":"email","type":"email","class":"pii","state":"masked","value":null,"display":"a***@***"}],"submitter_email":{...},"customer_id":{...},"customer_ip":{...}}. An answer that chose the Other option of its field carries one more key, `other_text`: the text the visitor typed, or null when none is stored or the answer is withheld. The answer `__other__` of a Product field names a product that is not in the catalog and carries the key the same way, with the name the visitor typed; no other answer has the key. update-values writes either answer as the pair {"value":"__other__","other_text":"…"} in place of the plain value; a Product field takes the pair only while its `is_allow_not_in_catalog` is on, and any other field refuses it. A pair whose value does not choose `__other__` is refused when its `other_text` holds a text, since the text would not be stored; `other_text` null or empty means no text was sent. The value of a Dynamic Grid answer is its rows; a row whose cell in a Product column is `__other__` names a product that is not in the catalog and carries the visitor's text under the key `<column code>:other_text`, beside that cell only. Only a Product column whose `allow_not_in_catalog` is "1" takes such a row. `state` is either `disclosed` or `masked`, and nothing else. Every entry, including the three system ones, carries the same envelope: `value` holds the real answer when the caller may see it and null when it is withheld, and the pseudonymized rendering travels separately in `display` (null once disclosed). A withheld value never occupies the `value` slot, so a client that copies `value` into its own records stores an absence it can act on rather than a mask it cannot tell apart from an answer. — JSON-encoded

linked_orders_json.description: Orders linked to the submission as a JSON array; null when the integration may not view orders. A `source` of `order_email` marks an order the visitor typed into an Order field, linked because the submission's email matches the order's email; the order was not picked from the customer's own list, so the visitor's identity and ownership of the order are not verified. — JSON-encoded

customer_group.description: What a set-approval did to an existing account's customer group (changed, pending, failed); needs PII access.

customer_group_text.description: The customer group outcome in a sentence; null with customer_group.

next_cursor.description: Opaque by contract; pass it back unchanged.

high_water_mark.description: The point up to which this feed is complete. Anything stamped later is withheld until it can be ordered safely, so a reader that stops here has missed nothing.

form_deleted.description: True when the form itself was deleted: every submission comes as "deleted". Read to the end, then drop your copy of the form.
